subproblem.title: Horizontal slices of a compatible form are compatible test forms: j_s^#(G^#ω) = (G∘j_s)^#ω
subproblem.statement: Let m, m′, q ∈ ℕ, let G : ℝ^{m+1} → ℝ^{m′} be C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞)), let ω be any q-form on ℝ^{m′} (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl m′) q; no regularity is assumed), θ ∈ D^q(ℝ^{m+1}), N ⊆ ℝ^{m+1} any set and s ∈ ℝ, and assume θ(y) = ω(G(y)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ G y) for every y ∈ N. Then there is θ_s ∈ D^q(ℝ^m) such that (i) θ_s(x)(v) = θ(cons(s, x))(i ↦ ι(v_i)) for all x ∈ ℝ^m and v : Fin q → ℝ^m, and (ii) θ_s(x) = ω(G_s(x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ G_s x) for every x ∈ ℝ^m with cons(s, x) ∈ N, where G_s := (fun x => G(cons(s, x))). Notation: ℝ^p := Eucl p = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p). For s ∈ ℝ and x ∈ ℝ^m, cons(s, x) := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons s (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ x)) ∈ ℝ^{m+1}; ι(v) := cons(0, v); e₀ := EuclideanSpace.single 0 1 ∈ ℝ^{m+1}; for y ∈ ℝ^{m+1}, t(y) := EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ y 0 and tl(y) := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ y)); cyl(A) := {y : t(y) ∈ [0,1] ∧ tl(y) ∈ A}. D_q(ℝ^p) := GeometricCurrentOn univ q, D^q(ℝ^p) := TestFormOn univ q, M = mass, spt = support, |γ| := covectorEuclideanNorm γ. For X ∈ D_q(ℝ^m) and Z ∈ D_{q+1}(ℝ^{m+1}), ProdChar(X, Z) means: for every η ∈ D^{q+1}(ℝ^{m+1}) and every φ : ℝ → D^q(ℝ^m) with φ(s)(x)(v) = η(cons(s, x))(Fin.cons e₀ (i ↦ ι(v_i))) for all s ∈ [0,1], x ∈ ℝ^m and v : Fin q → ℝ^m, one has Z(η) = ∫_0^1 X(φ(s)) ds (interval integral).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (m m' q : ℕ) (G : Eucl (m + 1) → Eucl m') (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl m') q) (θ : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Eucl (m + 1))) q) (N : Set (Eucl (m + 1))) (s : ℝ), ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) G → (∀ y ∈ N, (θ : DifferentialForm (Eucl (m + 1)) q) y = (ω (G y)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ G y)) → ∃ θs : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Eucl m)) q, (∀ (x : Eucl m) (v : Fin q → Eucl m), (θs : DifferentialForm (Eucl m) q) x v = (θ : DifferentialForm (Eucl (m + 1)) q) ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m + 1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons s (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ x))) (fun i => (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m + 1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons 0 (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ (v i))))) ∧ ∀ x : Eucl m, (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m + 1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons s (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ x)) ∈ N → (θs : DifferentialForm (Eucl m) q) x = (ω ((fun x : Eucl m => G ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m + 1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons s (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ x)))) x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ (fun x : Eucl m => G ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m + 1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons s (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ x)))) x)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: (Horizontal slices) and (Chain rule) in Part 0 of the supplied proof of dph_smooth_homotopy (4.1 of the source proof: j_s^#(G^#ω) = (G∘j_s)^#ω). Sibling used: compatible_form (iwl_sp_exists_compatible_testForm).

Notation: ℝ^p := Eucl p = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p). For s ∈ ℝ and x ∈ ℝ^m, cons(s, x) := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons s (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ x)) ∈ ℝ^{m+1}; ι(v) := cons(0, v); e₀ := EuclideanSpace.single 0 1 ∈ ℝ^{m+1}; for y ∈ ℝ^{m+1}, t(y) := EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ y 0 and tl(y) := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ y)); cyl(A) := {y : t(y) ∈ [0,1] ∧ tl(y) ∈ A}. D_q(ℝ^p) := GeometricCurrentOn univ q, D^q(ℝ^p) := TestFormOn univ q, M = mass, spt = support, |γ| := covectorEuclideanNorm γ. For X ∈ D_q(ℝ^m) and Z ∈ D_{q+1}(ℝ^{m+1}), ProdChar(X, Z) means: for every η ∈ D^{q+1}(ℝ^{m+1}) and every φ : ℝ → D^q(ℝ^m) with φ(s)(x)(v) = η(cons(s, x))(Fin.cons e₀ (i ↦ ι(v_i))) for all s ∈ [0,1], x ∈ ℝ^m and v : Fin q → ℝ^m, one has Z(η) = ∫_0^1 X(φ(s)) ds (interval integral). j_s(x) := cons(s, x) and G_s := G∘j_s = (x ↦ G(cons(s, x))). For a q-covector α and a continuous linear map L, α.compContinuousLinearMap L is the covector v ↦ α(i ↦ L(v_i)) (ContinuousAlternatingMap.compContinuousLinearMap_apply).

1. (The linear part ι.) Let ι : ℝ^m →L[ℝ] ℝ^{m+1} be the composition of the continuous linear map (0 : ℝ^m →L[ℝ] ℝ).finCons (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ) : ℝ^m →L[ℝ] (Fin (m+1) → ℝ), v ↦ Fin.cons 0 (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ v), with the continuous linear equivalence (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ).symm. By definition ι(v) = cons(0, v) for every v.
2. (Derivative of j_s.) For every x, HasFDerivAt j_s ι x: the map x ↦ Fin.cons s (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ x) has derivative (0).finCons (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ) at x (HasFDerivAt.finCons applied to hasFDerivAt_const s x and to the derivative of the continuous linear equivalence), and composing with the continuous linear equivalence (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ).symm (HasFDerivAt.comp) gives ι. Hence fderiv ℝ j_s x = ι for every x.
3. (j_s is a C^∞ isometry.) j_s(x) = ι(x) + j_s(0): after applying EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ both sides are (m+1)-tuples whose 0-th entries are s = 0 + s and whose (i+1)-th entries are x_i = x_i + 0 (case split with Fin.cases). Hence j_s is C^∞, as a continuous linear map plus a constant. Moreover ‖ι(v)‖ = ‖v‖, because ‖ι(v)‖² = 0² + Σ_i v_i² = ‖v‖² (EuclideanSpace.norm_eq, Fin.sum_univ_succ). Therefore dist(j_s x, j_s x′) = ‖ι(x − x′)‖ = ‖x − x′‖, so j_s is an isometry (Isometry.of_dist_eq), hence a closed embedding (Isometry.isClosedEmbedding; ℝ^m is complete), and j_s⁻¹(K) is compact for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^{m+1} (Topology.IsClosedEmbedding.isCompact_preimage).
4. (The slice is a test form.) Apply compatible_form with P := m, Q := m+1, j := q, U := univ, V := univ, A := univ, f := j_s and the test form θ ∈ D^q(ℝ^{m+1}) = TestFormOn univ q. Its hypotheses hold: univ is open, A ⊆ U, j_s is C^∞ (step 3), and j_s⁻¹(K) ∩ univ is compact for every compact K (step 3). We obtain θ_s ∈ TestFormOn univ q = D^q(ℝ^m) and an open N₀ ⊇ univ with θ_s(x) = θ(j_s x).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ j_s x) for every x ∈ N₀, that is, for every x. By step 2, θ_s(x) = θ(j_s x).compContinuousLinearMap ι for every x.
5. (Part (i).) For x ∈ ℝ^m and v : Fin q → ℝ^m, step 4 gives θ_s(x)(v) = θ(j_s x)(i ↦ ι(v_i)) = θ(cons(s, x))(i ↦ cons(0, v_i)).
6. (Chain rule.) G is C^∞, hence differentiable at j_s(x). With step 2, HasFDerivAt.comp gives HasFDerivAt G_s ((fderiv ℝ G (j_s x)).comp ι) x, so fderiv ℝ G_s x = (fderiv ℝ G (j_s x)).comp ι.
7. (Part (ii).) Let x satisfy cons(s, x) = j_s(x) ∈ N. By hypothesis θ(j_s x) = ω(G(j_s x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ G (j_s x)). By step 4, for every v: θ_s(x)(v) = θ(j_s x)(i ↦ ι(v_i)) = ω(G(j_s x))(i ↦ fderiv ℝ G (j_s x) (ι(v_i))) = ω(G_s(x))(i ↦ ((fderiv ℝ G (j_s x)).comp ι)(v_i)), and by step 6 the last expression equals (ω(G_s(x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ G_s x))(v). By extensionality, θ_s(x) = ω(G_s(x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ G_s x). ∎
proof_key_steps: j_s(x) = cons(s,x) is affine: j_s = ι + j_s(0) with ι(v) = cons(0,v) a linear isometry, so fderiv ℝ j_s = ι and j_s is C^∞ and proper (an isometric closed embedding).
compatible_form with f = j_s and U = V = A = univ gives θ_s ∈ D^q(ℝ^m) with θ_s(x) = θ(j_s x)∘ι everywhere, i.e. θ_s(x)(v) = θ(cons(s,x))(ι∘v).
Chain rule D(G∘j_s)(x) = DG(j_s x)∘ι; where θ = G^#ω, θ_s(x) = ω(G(j_s x))∘DG(j_s x)∘ι = (G∘j_s)^#ω(x).

audit.reason: The proof constructs the proper affine isometric inclusion, obtains its globally defined test-form pullback, and applies the chain rule. It proves both conclusions for arbitrary N and arbitrary ω without adding openness or regularity hypotheses.
